content.text: The text surveys ancient architecture from Assyria and Persia through Greece, Etruria, and Rome. Assyrian palaces at Khorsabad, Nineveh, and Nimroud were vast, terrace-based, richly sculptured, and largely wooden, while Persian builders adapted these forms in durable stone at Pasargadae, Persepolis, and Susa. It discusses Persian halls, tombs, temples, stairways, and decorative continuity with Assyria. The invention and development of arches are traced through Egypt, Assyria, Greece, and Rome. Greek architecture is presented through Pelasgic origins, Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian orders, temples, theatres, tombs, and harmonic proportions. Roman architecture fused Etruscan and Greek traditions, emphasizing arches, vaults, basilicas, baths, amphitheatres, triumphal monuments, and monumental tombs. Explicit narrative statements include: Daniel went to the garden; Sandra went to the office; Mary journeyed to the hallway.
